method: MIXED AND MOSTLY OPEN -- the best-sourced obstetric guideline in this compendium. S1 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP article on hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (December 2024 supplement), retrieved as HTML, tag-stripped and QUOTED VERBATIM INCLUDING ITS DOSE TABLE, so most of the drug doses here are machine re-checkable. A1-A4 are four AMH pages, paraphrased, no passage stored. The two sources are used for DIFFERENT THINGS: S1 for antenatal and postpartum management, which it covers and AMH does not, and AMH for magnesium sulfate, which S1 does not dose at all. Where they overlap -- the aspirin prophylaxis dose -- BOTH figures are stated and the difference is recorded rather than merged.

claims.claim: CHRONIC or pre-existing hypertension is high blood pressure diagnosed at any time BEFORE 20 weeks' gestation, or which does not resolve by 12 weeks postpartum

claims.claim: AMH gives aspirin for PREVENTION OF PRE-ECLAMPSIA as oral 75 TO 150 mg once daily, starting at 12 to 16 weeks gestation and continuing UNTIL DELIVERY; the indication is an ACCEPTED rather than an approved one, for women at moderate-to-high risk

claims.claim: AMH's hypertension topic gives a target BP below 135/85 mmHg for stable chronic, gestational or non-severe pre-eclampsia, with methyldopa, labetalol and nifedipine as first-line oral drugs and oral hydralazine also considered
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypertension' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/cardiovascular-drugs/antihypertensives/hypertension, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For severe hypertension in pregnancy, systolic above 160 or diastolic above 110 mmHg, oral nifedipine as a CONVENTIONAL TABLET AVAILABLE THROUGH THE SAS, and parenteral labetalol and hydralazine, are used for urgent BP reduction following local protocols
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypertension' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/cardiovascular-drugs/antihypertensives/hypertension, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
